predecessors.name: Golden Horde
predecessors.text: the steppe east of the Volga between the Volga and the Yaik (Ural), Edigu's Manghit ulus

successors.name: Crimean Khanate
successors.text: the Kuban steppe, Azov coast and Taman, 'Little Tartary' of the Lesser Nogai Horde

successors.name: Kalmyk Khanate
successors.text: the lower Volga steppe from which the Oirats expelled 'the majority of the native inhabitants, the Nogai Horde'

successors.name: Kazakh Khanate
successors.text: the Emba and Yaik steppe east of 52E

successors.name: Tsardom of Russia
successors.text: the Middle Volga steppe north of 47.6N, after the Samara fortress of 1586

ledger.x: 1450: the Manghit ulus of Edigu's descendants appears on Cliopatria's map as the Nogai Horde.
1520: the Kazakhs take the Nogai capital.
1521: the fighting for the south-east ends in the Kazakhs' favour.
1521: the Nogais lose the south-east steppe to the Kazakhs.
1557: the Lesser Nogai Horde founds itself along the Kuban.
1564: Cliopatria carries the state on as the 'Small Horde'.
1568: the Kazakhs defeat the Nogais at the Emba.
1572: the eastern steppe passes to the Kazakhs.
1572: the Azov and Kuban strip passes from the Crimean shape to the Small Horde.
1588: the Middle Volga steppe passes to Russia.
1588: the rest of the northern steppe falls out of the Horde's shape.
c. 1632: the Kalmyks break the first Nogai group. 'The first group was broken up circa 1632 by the Kalmyks.'

wars.name: Kasym Khan's capture of Saray-Juk (1520-1521)
wars.outcome: The Kazakhs under Kasym took the Nogai capital Saray-Juk in 1520 and drove the Nogais west across the Volga; Cliopatria gives the south-east steppe to the Kazakhs in 1521.

wars.name: Crimean attack on Astrakhan (1523)
wars.outcome: '1523 Crimea briefly takes Astrakhan, but its army and Khan are destroyed by the Nogais'; the Nogais killed Khan Mehmed I Giray.

wars.name: Russian conquest of Kazan and Astrakhan (1552, 1556)
Kazakh-Nogai war of Haqnazar (1568-1577)
wars.outcome: The Kazakhs defeated the Nogai Horde at the Emba in 1568 (Kazakh Khanate page; the Haqnazar Khan page says 1570) and Haqnazar captured the Horde's capital Saraychik in 1577; Cliopatria gives the eastern steppe to the Kazakhs in 1572.

wars.name: Kalmyk conquest of the Nogai steppe (c. 1632-1634)
wars.outcome: The first Nogai group was 'broken up circa 1632 by the Kalmyks' and a major Nogai defeat followed in 1634; the Oirats expelled most Nogais from the lower Volga, some fled to the North Caucasus and the Black Sea steppe, some became Oirat vassals, others sought…

wars.name: Kalmyk and Russian expeditions against the Kuban Nogais (1711, 1735)

certainty.note: Steppe pastoral frontiers throughout; no treaty line is known for any Nogai border.
